items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept concealed?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires diligent effort
The context is the mortal world among base people
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching rightfully be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
This is the fifth chapter
The chapter is concluded here
items.inference: The fifth chapter of the text emerged from Candradvīpa ends here.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of Kaula been understood?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Understanding arose by that lord's grace
The object understood is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: The speaker has understood the determination of Kaula through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have understood the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve according to this teaching?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
The speaker requests a complete explanation
items.inference: The speaker asks to be told fully where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality being described?
premises: The subject is identified as supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The ultimate reality is supreme, partless, eternal, and untainted.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to haṃsa and śakti?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is identified as the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.
uncertainties: The precise sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul who is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
It is situated within beings
This applies to all living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement of saṃsthitam with vāyuḥ is unusual in form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is ascribed to the soul upon leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
At that point the soul is named
It is called supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and perceived according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes down through tradition
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as it has come down through traditional succession.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the effect of merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing itself is presented as sufficient
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even the mere hearing of this knowledge has a significant effect.
uncertainties: The sentence continues into the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner undertakes the ochre state
That state is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices the bondage-free ochre discipline for six months attains its result.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to renunciation or an ochre-robed state.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months in the ochre state, free from bondage...

items.question: What benefits result from sustained practice of this discipline?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains union with yogis
These are outcomes of the prescribed practice
items.inference: The practice leads to freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: ...becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī
The subject is the practice concerning the soul
This teaching has been told to her
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: What qualities qualify a person to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The case difference between genitive and locative recipients is notable.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firmly resolved mind.

items.question: To whom must the essential Kaula teaching not be given?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly valued
Its origin is associated with the yoginīs
Giving it is explicitly prohibited in this context
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The exact scope of the prohibition is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after receiving knowledge?
premises: The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
A change is asserted now
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: The speaker claims that her body, once veiled by ignorance, is now pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What further auspicious teaching does the speaker wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear
The topic concerns time
The desired teaching is the auspicious overcoming of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious teaching on overcoming time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or overcoming depending on context.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious teaching on overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is no doubt in the teaching
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The speaker assures without doubt that death can be destroyed and will explain how.
items.plain_english: I will tell you; there is no doubt, as to how death is destroyed.

items.question: What intense experience affects even the wise practitioner at the nectar point?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar
The means involves the essence of juice
Even the wise one experiences burning
items.inference: Even a wise practitioner may feel burning at the nectar point through the essence of juice.
uncertainties: The physiological referents of nectar and juice are esoteric.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one may feel burning at the tip of nectar by the essence of the juice.

items.question: How should the practitioner perform the breath-drinking technique to overcome time?
premises: The action is focused at the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner should draw in the air
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly drink the air at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink the air.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The condition is sustained practice
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this technique destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What protection against poison is claimed for the accomplished practitioner?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the practitioner's body.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
